posts.caption:
SIBO isn't always about overgrowth—and that's the part most people never get told.

In my telehealth functional medicine clinic, I see it all the time. Someone's been taking every anti-bacterial supplement, eliminated half their diet, and still feels bloated, gassy, and stuck. Why? Because their SIBO might not be a bacterial problem at all.

Here's the physiology: small intestinal bacterial overgrowth happens when bacteria linger in the small intestine instead of moving through it. That's a *motility* problem—not necessarily an overgrowth problem. Your small intestine has a built-in cleaning wave called the migrating motor complex (MMC). When it stalls (from stress, low stomach acid, food sensitivity, dysbiosis, or slow transit), bacteria set up camp. They ferment poorly digested food, and you get the bloating, gas, and symptoms you're experiencing.

The reframe? Instead of asking "How do I kill the bacteria?", we ask "Why is transit slow?" That changes everything. We look at stomach acid, bile flow, motility patterns, food sensitivities, and the health of your gut barrier—not just the bacterial count.

The good news: once you restore normal motility and address the root cause, the bacteria naturally clear.

Drop a comment SIBO below for a free functional-medicine guide to small intestinal clearance—or swipe to see the foods and herbs that genuinely support transit.

#SIBO #FunctionalMedicine #GutHealth #MotiityMatters #AdelaideWellness
